stops.note: Brazilian slang meaning "a trend" or "flair" (literally 'bump', from French bosse)

literally "new trend", a mellow fusion of samba and jazz; João Gilberto's 1958 recording of Jobim and Vinicius de Moraes's 'Chega de Saudade' launched the style, and the 1959 lyrics of 'Desafinado' name it
Stan Getz and Charlie Byrd's album Jazz Samba and a Carnegie Hall concert in November 1962 started a US craze; João Gilberto and Tom Jobim's 'The Girl from Ipanema' of 1964 made it a global hit
stops.meaning: a mellow Brazilian music genre blending samba and jazz

current_meaning: a mellow, jazz-influenced style of Brazilian popular music
